packages.notes: Support for the Bambu Lab CyberBrick Time-lapse Kit: plugged into a free 6-pin bus port on an AMS, the kit stays linked (its light shows solid green) and OpenAMS fires it from Klipper with CYBERBRICK_SHOT or M1004 S5 P1. The bridge also no longer mistakes another device on the bus for an AMS HT that stopped answering, and its diagnostics now count one kind of transmit fault they used to miss.

The bridge can be updated with filament loaded: cortex-bridge.py update holds the AMS followers off for the update, and they come back afterwards. The bridge also reports its version while an AMS is working, so status shows it with filament loaded. An AMS that asks for a bus index when none is free no longer holds up the other AMS for seconds at a time. A dryer command cut short when the bridge lost control of the bus no longer blocks later dryer starts and stops until a restart. After a bridge restart, an unload still works when the filament has already been pulled out of the hub. A tag read waits while an AMS HT runs a dry it started itself, and a dryer request the bridge turns down reports the reason at once instead of a timeout 5 seconds later.

The bridge tells OpenAMS every 2 seconds whether each AMS is reachable, not only when it changes. Before, if one of those reports went missing, OpenAMS could keep showing an AMS as unreachable until a FIRMWARE_RESTART.

An AMS 2 Pro that answers at an index meant for an AMS HT (an older bridge firmware could leave it there, and it keeps that index through power cycles) is used at that index instead of being refused. Before, the bridge refused it on every start and no AMS came online.

A dry whose target is below the AMS's current chamber temperature (a box still warm from an earlier dry) starts and cools toward its target instead of being stopped at once as overheating. An overheating dryer is now reported as chamber_overtemperature.
OpenAMS sees each AMS's own filament odometer as its encoder: the distance from park the AMS reports, counting up as it feeds and back to 0 at park. Before, the encoder always read 0.

Two AMS units of the same kind (two AMS HTs, or two AMS 2 Pros) each report their own dryer status again: target, time left and vent position. Before, both showed the vents as unknown and no time left while they dried.

A fault clear (OAMS_CLEAR_FAULT) on an idle AMS now also sends the printer's retry sequence, which resets slot lights a past fault left in its error pattern after the error itself went back to 0. Such a clear takes about 2.5 s; a drying or moving AMS is cleared as before.

After a bridge restart the bridge finds every AMS that kept its bus index before it offers one to an AMS asking for an index, so two AMS units no longer end up answering at the same index. An AMS whose answers stopped matching its identity (two units answered at its index) is identified again and comes back online by itself, with its firmware version read again.

After a host stall trips the bridge's host watchdog (a slow print start, for example), each AMS reconnects by itself, without FIRMWARE_RESTART, and OpenAMS re-arms its follower; after any restart the follower comes back only when OpenAMS re-arms it, so update OpenAMS with this firmware. AMS units that read their own tags can send OpenAMS each read in full.

After an AMS or the bridge restarts with filament still loaded (a power cycle, an AMS or bridge firmware update), the bridge picks the loaded spool up again by itself, so the next print keeps feeding with the AMS's assist instead of reporting a runout. The AMS HT reports one consistent filament sensor reading.

An AMS HT on its firmware 04.x or later dries with filament loaded and keeps feeding a print, and can be loaded while it dries (without Rotate). The bridge updates an AMS's own firmware, upgrade or downgrade (cortex-bridge.py ams-firmware update), with Bambu Lab's own image you download, and resumes an AMS left waiting in its loader without a power cycle.

Clear errors now clears what used to need a power cycle: an AMS that still reports moving is stopped first, a bay pulled back by hand is forgotten so drying and tag reads work again, and a clear during a dryer stop waits for it instead of being refused.
An AMS 2 Pro or AMS HT can turn its spools while it dries, as a Bambu printer does: tick Rotate spools while drying in Mainsail, or add ROTATE=1 to OAMS_DRYER_START. Unload the AMS first.

Unloads no longer stall on an AMS 1: the AMS rewinds its spool only once OpenAMS says the filament is out of the extruder, a retry after a failed unload starts the same way, and a failure names the AMS's own error.

During an unload the AMS works with the extruder instead of against it: an AMS 1 now pulls the filament back as the extruder retracts (it never feeds it forward), and every AMS reports reverse following only once it is actually pulling back. A working AMS is never refused.

An unload whose filament does not move back (a cut that did not sever it) stops the AMS within seconds and says so, instead of pulling for a minute; an AMS's own jam during a load is reported as a jam.
An AMS 2 Pro is only asked to dry when it is idle with no filament in its hub, and a dry it does not start is reported within 10 s instead of going unnoticed.
During a dry the bridge asks the AMS to vent as a Bambu printer does, so the vents open once the chamber is at temperature; the AMS HT's vent position shows in Klipper.

During a dry the vents open once the chamber is at temperature and the moisture stops rising, and the dry ends with the vents closed until it cools; an AMS connected while the bridge runs is added at once.
When no AMS answers, status and the support report say why: a silent cable, data that can't be read, or an AMS turned away, with the reason.
The AMS measures its filament path (OAMS_CALIBRATE_PTFE_LENGTH), every load reports the path it measured, and a load that stops says why.
Stock AMS 1: loads at full speed to the toolhead (about 12 s instead of 17 s) and reads Bambu spool tags.
Stock AMS 1 support: it connects, reports its bay sensors and relays the buffer, so it loads and unloads.
